answer: Make identity costly to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent locks a time-bonded stake before trading, and reputation accrues only through attested work. A shared ledger acts like a prism, refracting one agent's record across many witnesses, so a forged history cannot pass. Trust is like basalt: dense, slow to form, hard to counterfeit. Newcomers enter through a narrow jetty, with limited permissions and peer review until stake and history prove them. A sybil operator can spawn thousands of identities, but each must pay the stake and survive scrutiny, so costs scale while gains stay flat.
